title: Why Worship Is Warfare
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: From the very first episode: worship drives out other loves, puts us on offense, and sets our minds on things above.
exhortation: Welcome to the very first episode. We're starting with Ephesians 6:13. Here are three reasons worship is warfare.

First, worship drives out all other loves. It's an offensive weapon. We often focus so much on fighting sin that we forget to fill our hearts with Christ. But a heart is never truly empty. It is filled either with the world or with God's Spirit. True holiness isn't found in a vacuum of not sinning, but in a heart so captivated by the glory of Jesus that there's no room left for competing affections. Like a cup pressed down and running over, a Spirit-filled life naturally displaces worldliness by the sheer volume of God's presence.

Second, worship puts us on offense. It isn't a retreat. It's an advance. In spiritual warfare, a defensive position is a losing position. If you only play defense, you're just waiting to be starved out by the enemy. The Christian life is designed for mission and momentum. When we put God's praises on our lips at the start of every morning, we move from protecting ground to taking new ground.

And finally, worship sets our minds on things above. It puts us in a heavenly mindset from the start. A holy Christian is a bold Christian, because he is no longer preoccupied with self-preservation. When your mind is set on things above and your day begins with praise, you move from holding on to pressing forward. We don't settle for where we are. We advance the kingdom by keeping our eyes fixed on the King.
prayer: Lord, what an amazing thing it is to be loved by you this way, and to be raised with you in righteousness and glory.

Help us remember as we go through our day that you have paid the price. We don't need to wallow in our sin or retreat. We need to run to you and repent, because in you are mercy, grace, forgiveness and victory. Amen.
